sentences.text: As per the appellant, on 28.01.2021, she along with her husband Dalpat Singh was going on a motorcycle from Pipliyamandi to her village Peerguradiya.

When they reached Badri Fanta, a car bearing Registration No. MP-14-CC-3981 being driven by respondent No.1, owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.3 came from wrong direction and dashed against their motorcycle as a result of which they fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
They were taken to the hospital for treatment.
The appellant had suffered a fracture in her right leg which was operated upon and a rod was fitted therein.
She remained in the hospital for a period of five days.

03. Thereafter, the appellant filed an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.20,60,000/- to her by way of compensation for the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 by filing written statement to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties, the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.

04. This appeal has been preferred by the appellant for enhancement of compensation on the ground that the disability assessed by the Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:325 3 MA-6619-2024 Tribunal was only 5% whereas as per the treating doctor himself, the same was 7%.
The appellant had suffered a fracture in her right tibia fibula bone and a rod had been inserted therein.
The permanent disability hence could not have been assessed at 5%.
It is further submitted that the income of the appellant has been assessed at Rs.4,000/- per month only.

Even if she was considered to be a housewife, then also in accordance with the relevant guidelines of the Collector and the guidelines issued by the NALSA, her income ought to have been assessed appropriately.

05. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 has submitted that just and appropriate amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant in which there is no illegality in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
06. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.

07. The doctor who had treated the appellant namely Dr. P.K. Upadhyay was examined before the Claims Tribunal and he had proved the Disability Certificate given by him to the appellant in which it was stated that she has suffered overall permanent disability to the tune of 7%.
The Claims Tribunal has however taken the permanent disability at 5% only.
Since the appellant had suffered fracture in her right tibia fibula bone and a rod had been inserted therein, the disability could not have been assessed at 5%.
In doing so, the Claims Tribunal has acted illegally.
The permanent disability is hence assessed at 7%.

08. Even if the appellant was considered to be a housewife then also in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:325 4 MA-6619-2024 view of the applicable guidelines her income could not have been assessed at a meager amount of Rs.4,000/- per month.
The same ought to have been assessed at Rs.8,400/- per month since the accident had taken place on 28.01.2021.

2 09.

sentences.text: The amount which the appellant would be entitled for the permanent disability suffered by her would consequently be Rs.8,400/- x 7% x 12 x 15 + 25% for future prospects of rise in income.
The same would hence come to Rs.1,32,300/-.
The appellant remained under treatment for a period of about three months, hence her loss of income would come to Rs.8,400/- x 3 i.e. Rs.25,200/-.
The other amounts awarded by the Claims Tribunal in respect of medical bills, special diet, attendant and conveyance are just and appropriate and do not call for any interference.

10. Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion, the appellant is held entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.2,08,529/- to her by way of compensation whereas the Claims Tribunal has awarded her a sum of Rs.1,13,029/- only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.95,500/- which shall be payable to her along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE Shilpa Smt. Sushila vs Manav on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17374672/
